title: Meaning trial V5: wallet and ledger, the tool's own echoes
instructions: For each item decide whether the ECHO says exactly the same thing as the RULE: no more, no less. Some do and some do not. Judge every item on its own. What the brief calls a default or a fixed convention is not a difference.

parts.title: Rules and echoes
parts.question: Each item has an English RULE and the tool's ECHO of how it understood the rule. Is the echo a faithful reading of the rule?

items.first: A rejected transfer never changes the ledger
items.second:
Applies to: a transfer: every ledger, every transfer (sender->receiver:amount, two usize account numbers and a u64 amount)
    ONLY rejected calls [asked for]
Assuming: nothing: every state and every input
Then: the sum of the balances of every account of the ledger after the call equals the sum of the balances of every account of the ledger before it
Accepted: an acceptance is the answer yes (true); the answer no is a rejection
Defaults: D3 before / after one call: 'unchanged', 'increased by' and the like compare the state before one call with the state after it, not states in between
    D4 for all values: every outline <parameter>, every state and every input is universally quantified at the front; the Examples rows are instances
Not default: ONLY rejected calls are covered (asked for by 'rejected' / 'if it is rejected'); calls that are accepted, or that give no answer, are outside this clause

items.first: A transfer for which the amount of the transfer is more than the balance of account the sender of the transfer of the ledger is always rejected
items.second:
Applies to: a transfer: every ledger, every transfer (sender->receiver:amount, two usize account numbers and a u64 amount)
    every such call, accepted or rejected [default D2]
Assuming: nothing: every state and every input
Then: the call gives an answer [default D1]
    it is NOT the case that the answer is an acceptance (see `accepted`)
Accepted: an acceptance is the answer yes (true); the answer no is a rejection
Defaults: D1 always answers: the call must return an answer for every input the reading applies to (no panic, no abort, no endless loop)
    D2 rejected calls are covered: the reading applies to every call, whether the operation accepts or rejects it
    D4 for all values: every outline <parameter>, every state and every input is universally quantified at the front; the Examples rows are instances

items.first: A batch applied as a whole agrees with the same batch applied transfer by transfer and kept only if every transfer is applied
items.second:
Applies to: a batch applied as a whole: every ledger, every batch (a list of transfers, in order)
    every such call, accepted or rejected [default D2]
Assuming: nothing: every state and every input
Then: the call gives an answer [default D1]
    the answer and the state after the call are exactly what the same batch applied transfer by transfer (the operation `apply_batch` of the same code) and kept only if every transfer is applied (accepted, with the ledger that leaves, if it applies every transfer of the batch; otherwise rejected, with the ledger left as it was) gives for the state before and the input
Defaults: D1 always answers: the call must return an answer for every input the reading applies to (no panic, no abort, no endless loop)
    D2 rejected calls are covered: the reading applies to every call, whether the operation accepts or rejects it
    D4 for all values: every outline <parameter>, every state and every input is universally quantified at the front; the Examples rows are instances

items.first: A successful transfer never changes the ledger
items.second:
Applies to: a transfer: every ledger, every transfer (sender->receiver:amount, two usize account numbers and a u64 amount)
    ONLY successful calls [asked for]
Assuming: nothing: every state and every input
Then: the balances of the ledger, account by account after the call equals the balances of the ledger, account by account before it
Accepted: an acceptance is the answer yes (true); the answer no is a rejection
Defaults: D3 before / after one call: 'unchanged', 'increased by' and the like compare the state before one call with the state after it, not states in between

items.first: A transfer is accepted whenever the transfer is valid on the ledger
items.second:
Applies to: a transfer: every ledger, every transfer (sender->receiver:amount, two usize account numbers and a u64 amount)
    every such call, accepted or rejected [default D2]
Assuming: nothing: every state and every input
Then: the call gives an answer [default D1]
    if the transfer can be carried out exactly on the ledger (both accounts exist and differ, the sender covers the amount, the receiver's balance stays within 2^64 - 1), then the answer is an acceptance (see `accepted`) (and the call gives an answer whether or not the transfer can be carried out exactly on the ledger (both accounts exist and differ, the sender covers the amount, the receiver's balance stays within 2^64 - 1))
Accepted: an acceptance is the answer yes (true); the answer no is a rejection
Defaults: D1 always answers: the call must return an answer for every input the reading applies to (no panic, no abort, no endless loop)
    D2 rejected calls are covered: the reading applies to every call, whether the operation accepts or rejects it
    D4 for all values: every outline <parameter>, every state and every input is universally quantified at the front; the Examples rows are instances
    D8 conditions are read before the call: what 'assuming', 'for which', 'whenever', 'only if' and 'exactly when' say about the state is judged on the state before the call (of a sequence: before its first call), not on any state the call passes through or leaves

items.first: A batch followed by a computation of the total is accepted exactly when the total of the balances of the ledger is at most the maximum
items.second:
Applies to: a batch followed by a computation of the total: every ledger, every batch (a list of transfers, in order)
    every such call, accepted or rejected [default D2]
Assuming: nothing: every state and every input
Then: the call gives an answer [default D1]
    the answer is an acceptance (see `accepted`) if and only if the sum of the balances of every account of the ledger is at most the largest total that can be reported (2^64 - 1)
    (of a sequence: every call in it must answer; the answer spoken of is the LAST call's)
Accepted: an acceptance is an answer that carries a value; an answer with no value is a rejection
Defaults: D1 always answers: the call must return an answer for every input the reading applies to (no panic, no abort, no endless loop)
    D2 rejected calls are covered: the reading applies to every call, whether the operation accepts or rejects it
    D4 for all values: every outline <parameter>, every state and every input is universally quantified at the front; the Examples rows are instances
    D8 conditions are read before the call: what 'assuming', 'for which', 'whenever', 'only if' and 'exactly when' say about the state is judged on the state before the call (of a sequence: before its first call), not on any state the call passes through or leaves
